newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish generals step up pressure on Erbakan.
newsitem.headline: Turkish generals step up pressure on Erbakan.

text.p: Turkey's powerful military has stepped up pressure on beleaguered Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan in a row over the role of religion in politics.

Newspapers on Monday quoted leading general Erol Ozkasnak as implicitly denying the military was working in close cooperation with Erbakan -- just one day after the prime minister played down any rift with the secularist army commanders.

"The Turkish armed forces is in harmony with those who believe in the republic...and the implementation of its basic principles. It is not, and cannot be, in harmony with anyone else," the Sabah newspaper quoted Ozkasnak as saying.
Other papers carried the same quotes, which Turkish political analysts said were a clear reference to the friction between the military and Erbakan's Islamists.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, had said on Saturday he was "in complete harmony" with the army despite an anti-Islamist warning by the military.
The generals, who regard Erbakan as a threat to official secularism, told the government last week to clamp down on Islamist activists.

Erbakan was to meet two leftist opposition leaders on Monday for talks on the latest political situation, his office said in a statement. The prime minister was also due to meet main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz later in the week.
The army briefly sent tanks onto the streets of an Islamist district of Ankara last month after anti-secularist protest there attended by the Iranian ambassador.
